_doc: Single machine-readable source of truth for backend selection.
Each capability lists candidate backends in PREFERENCE ORDER. A backend is usable only if
every path in `requires` resolves to an object with .available == true in ENVIRONMENT.json.
`agreement` records what was MEASURED against the certified MNE reference — not asserted.

Numbers come from the fixed public snapshot: https://github.com/dengzhe-hou/auto-eeg-analysis/blob/995f53d42cc74205b164e8711d4b289b8c2ad3a1/tools/benchmark/CROSS_TOOLBOX_RESULT.json (see CROSS_TOOLBOX_EVAL.md in the same snapshot).
Where nothing was measured the field says so; a resolver must not imply equivalence it
`pin` is the load-bearing field. Cross-toolbox agreement is NOT a property of the toolbox —
it is a property of how completely the specification is pinned. Leaving any listed convention
to the toolbox default produced per-subject divergence of up to 43% of the group effect
(CROSS_TOOLBOX_EVAL.md sec 2). A backend must therefore never be selected without also
emitting its `pin` list into the generated code.
Adding a backend requires: a probe entry in tools/env/check_env.{sh,ps1}, an entry here, and
either measured agreement or an explicit `"measured": false`. tools/tests/test_backends.py

mne.label: MNE-Python
mne.notes: The certified reference. The recorded tools/validation/*_results.json in the fixed public snapshot were produced here.

eeglab.label: EEGLAB (MATLAB or GNU Octave)
eeglab.notes: Validated under Octave 10.3; MATLAB assumed equivalent but not verified.

fieldtrip.label: FieldTrip (MATLAB or GNU Octave)
fieldtrip.notes: Validated with FieldTrip 20170830 under Octave 10.3. Newer releases may change defaults.

erp.preprocess_average.description: Filter, re-reference, epoch, baseline-correct and average an ERP contrast.

with_fully_pinned_spec.note: Pinning the FieldTrip filter specification (cutoff convention AND transition width together) took max|d| from 0.721 to 0.050 uV; the cutoff-convention-only step at a fixed 0.1 Hz transition width is 0.802 -> 0.050 uV. Staged comparison -- not attributable to one parameter alone.

pin.question: Does the stated band edge name the passband edge or the -6 dB point?
pin.mne: passband edge; -6 dB sits half a transition band below
pin.eeglab: passband edge; -6 dB sits half a transition band below
pin.consequence: Unpinned, 'a 0.1 Hz high-pass' is a 2x different filter across toolboxes. Worst-case per-subject error 0.721 uV = 43% of the P3 group effect.

pin.question: How wide is the FIR transition band at each edge?
pin.mne: auto: max(l_freq*0.25, 2) capped at l_freq for the low edge; max(h_freq*0.25, 2) for the high edge
pin.eeglab: 0.1 Hz at both edges by pop_eegfiltnew's heuristic
pin.consequence: Changes filter length ~2x. On its own it explained none of the observed P3 divergence, but it sets the -6 dB offset that cutoff_convention depends on, so the two must be pinned together.

pin.question: Is the amplitude threshold peak-to-peak or absolute?
pin.fieldtrip: no idiomatic default; must be written explicitly
pin.consequence: Unpinned, the two retain different trial sets. Harmonizing it improved per-subject agreement 2.2x (mean |d| 0.089 -> 0.040 uV).

pin.question: Which resampling algorithm?
pin.eeglab: signal-package resample, or a cubic-spline fallback when Octave Forge signal is absent
pin.fieldtrip: ft_resampledata (needs Octave Forge signal); decimation is exact when the data are already band-limited below the new Nyquist
pin.consequence: Not isolated by any experiment. After the filter was fully pinned the residual P3 disagreement was 0.05 uV, which bounds this term without attributing it.

eeglab.reason: The ICLabel plugin implements the same published network as mne-icalabel, but AEA has not benchmarked them against each other. Do not present them as numerically interchangeable.

pin.question: Is the input average-referenced before ICLabel?
pin.consequence: Non-average-referenced input silently degrades classification rather than erroring.

stats.cluster_permutation.description: Cluster-based permutation test over channels x time.

mne.evidence: used by every recorded validation script in the fixed public snapshot

fieldtrip.caveat: FieldTrip's clusterstat needs spm_bwlabel, unavailable to Octave; a pure-Octave connected-component labeller verified against scipy.ndimage.label (12/12) is supplied. FieldTrip still contributes the statistic, threshold, permutation scheme and p-value.

elementwise.supported_wording: machine-precision-equal t-maps; exactly identical cluster partitions

shipped_configuration.note: certified at the validation scripts' own configuration: component window, one-sided default threshold (MNE threshold=None == FieldTrip clusteralpha 0.05 one-tailed)

pin.question: What exact cluster-forming threshold does 'alpha = 0.05, one-sided' become?
pin.mne: default (threshold=None) for tail=+/-1 is one-sided: t.ppf(0.95, df); a two-tailed critical value only when tail=0, or when the caller passes one explicitly
pin.fieldtrip: cfg.clusteralpha is one-tailed when cfg.tail is set: t.ppf(alpha, df) -- the same convention as MNE's one-sided default
pin.consequence: The toolboxes' defaults agree. The 18-vs-14 cluster discrepancy in CLUSTER_CERT.md arose because the certification script passed t.ppf(0.975, df) = 2.093 explicitly to MNE while FieldTrip used 1.729 -- an author-side reading of the phrase, not a toolbox default. With the threshold pinned the two implementations give exactly identical cluster partitions and machine-precision-equal t-maps (ELEMENTWISE_*.json). Always write the threshold as a number (or 'one-sided 0.95 quantile'), never as 'alpha = 0.05'.

pin.question: What seed, and how many permutations?
pin.consequence: Cluster p-values are not reproducible without both.

pin.question: Cluster-forming threshold and adjacency definition.
pin.mne: t at p<0.05 for the actual df; channel adjacency from the montage
pin.consequence: Different adjacency graphs give different clusters from identical data.
